subject.title: fix(agents): memoize exec auto-reviewer verdicts for identical requests (#102249)

question: Should a model-issued low-risk `allow-once` verdict be reusable only for gateway requests bound to the same resolved executable, while node requests remain per-call reviewed?
rationale: Reusing a nominally single-use authorization changes the exec trust boundary, and current node requests cannot express the executable identity required by the gateway contract; automation should not choose a broader authorization policy.

options.title: Gateway-only exact binding
options.body: Cache only completed low-risk gateway verdicts with a non-empty `resolvedPath`, include it in the key, and keep node reviews uncached.

options.title: Extend node identity first
options.body: Add a canonical resolved-executable field to the node preparation protocol before enabling memoization for either host.

options.title: Keep per-call review
options.body: Do not memoize authorization verdicts and accept the repeated reviewer cost until a broader trust model is approved.

recommendation.title: Gateway-only exact binding
recommendation.body: Cache only completed low-risk gateway verdicts with a non-empty `resolvedPath`, include it in the key, and keep node reviews uncached.

likelyOwner.reason: As repository owner, this is the best available routing candidate for an explicit exec-authorization policy choice.
